About the Team
OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineeriIng teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works. Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role
As an Enterprise Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations. This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.
This role is based in our SF or NYC office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:
• Partner directly with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

• Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

• Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

• Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

• Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

• Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

• Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

• Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:
• Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

• Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering—not only program or stakeholder management.

• Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

• Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

• Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

• Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

• Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

• Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.

• Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

A World-Changing Company

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

Mission Manager is Palantir’s PaaS for enabling US Government customers and vendors to run software securely and compliantly in the most sensitive environments, but without the overhead — whether connected, disconnected, cloud, or edge. Built on the strength of Palantir’s Apollo platform, it provides the critical infrastructure needed to rapidly onboard and deploy applications into a secure Kubernetes-based ecosystem, freeing our customers to focus on building and powering mission-critical systems.

The Mission Manager offering is still in its earliest days, and by joining us now, you’ll define the strategy for how we develop and scale it — witnessing firsthand the impact of your work on critical missions and the new capabilities you unlock. You’ll drive this by building elegant, robust APIs powered by Kubernetes controllers, bridging the gap between a raw Kubernetes cluster and a fully featured, infrastructure-agnostic runtime that can meet the operational demands of hundreds of specialized microservices. You’ll undertake this challenge alongside an energized team with a wide array of backgrounds and skillsets, all united by an ambitious vision for what’s possible.

About the Team
OpenAI Consumer Devices is building the next generation of products that bring powerful AI into people’s everyday lives. Guided by OpenAI’s mission to ensure AGI benefits all of humanity, our team combines world-class researchers, engineers, designers, and operators who care deeply about creating useful, intuitive, and responsible technology. You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside exceptional people on ambitious, zero-to-one challenges at the intersection of hardware, software, and AI. This is a chance to help define an entirely new category of products—and shape how people experience AI in the future.
Our team works across custom silicon, embedded systems, operating systems, and cloud services to build reliable consumer devices and the platforms behind them. We connect kernel development with the broader software stack to deliver complete product capabilities.

About the Role
As an Operating Systems Engineer focused on the Linux kernel, you will design, develop, and maintain the kernel capabilities that underpin OpenAI’s consumer devices. You’ll bring deep expertise in one or more Linux kernel subsystems and carry solutions through the higher-level software stack.
Your ownership will extend into the userspace services, libraries, tools, and interfaces needed to deliver complete product features. You’ll shape the boundaries between kernel and userspace, make design decisions across the stack, and see your work through development, integration, and production.

In this role, you will:
• Build kernel capabilities: Design, implement, and maintain Linux kernel subsystem changes that support device capabilities and product requirements.

• Own features across the stack: Choose appropriate kernel and userspace boundaries, and build the interfaces and supporting components needed to deliver reliable features in shipped products.

• Debug complex system behavior: Use tracing, profiling, instrumentation, and diagnostic tools to resolve correctness, concurrency, performance, power, and reliability issues in development and production.

• Measure and validate improvements: Develop tests and representative workloads to demonstrate repeatable performance, power, and reliability gains and detect regressions across kernel and userspace.

• Partner across disciplines: Work with hardware, firmware, platform, and application engineers to turn system requirements into understandable, maintainable solutions.

• Contribute sustainable kernel changes: Prepare reviewable patches, incorporate feedback, and contribute fixes and improvements upstream where appropriate. Maintain product-specific changes responsibly as the kernel evolves.

Minimum Qualifications
• Substantial hands-on experience designing, developing, and debugging one or more Linux kernel subsystems, such as memory management, storage, networking, high-speed peripherals, power management, scheduling, or virtualization.

• Proficiency in C for kernel and low-level systems development.

• Strong understanding of kernel concurrency, synchronization, memory ownership, and resource lifetimes.

• Experience delivering systems capabilities across kernel and userspace, including designing interfaces and diagnosing problems that cross that boundary.

• Understanding of Linux kernel development principles and practices: maintainable designs, appropriate abstractions, reviewable patches, compatibility awareness, and careful validation to prevent regressions.

You might thrive in this role if you:
• Are proficient in Rust for systems programming, with experience developing Linux kernel code in Rust alongside C.

• Participate in the Linux community through patches, code review, testing, bug reports, technical discussions, or collaboration with subsystem maintainers.

• Take ownership of complete solutions and follow problems across system boundaries.

• Make careful tradeoffs among functionality, security, performance, power, and maintainability, and explain your decisions with evidence.

Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers, sharp problem-solvers and builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. Private markets have been closed to everyday investors for decades. The Capital Markets team is opening them. As the Product Manager for this team you will own the products that give retail investors access to companies before they reach the public markets including:

• IPO Access, which distributes pre-IPO share allocations to our customers

• Robinhood Ventures, our family of publicly traded funds holding direct positions in the world’s best private companies

• New products you will define to give investors direct access to individual private companies and alternative investments.

As a Senior Product Manager on Capital Markets, you will own these product lines end to end and help shape where all three go next. You’ll own the strategy and products that help everyday investors access IPOs, Private Companies, Alternatives and more. You'll work with our top tier engineers, designers, researchers, data scientists, and investing team to ship industry-changing products that revolutionize access to private markets. Today private markets are the largest category of assets ordinary investors cannot touch. This is a chance to change that.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA or New York, NY offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you'll do

• Own the strategy, roadmap, and execution for one of the Capital Markets product lines - IPO Access, Robinhood Ventures, or single-asset private offerings - and contribute to the strategy across all three

• Lead 0-1 launches, including the in-app experience for investing in a single private asset and the discovery surfaces that make private markets navigable for a first-time investor

• Translate ambiguous regulatory, operational, and partner requirements into clear, dependable customer experiences, working shoulder to shoulder with legal, compliance, and operations

• Build and manage relationships with external partners - issuers, underwriters, fund administrators, and infrastructure vendors - so that a shared product actually ships

• Set the quality bar for a product line where a confusing flow costs customers real money and real trust

• Use research, experimentation, and product analytics to decide what to build, and to prove what worked

• Communicate strategy, tradeoffs, and the reasoning behind them to senior leadership

What you bring

• 5+ years of product management experience building and shipping high-quality consumer or consumer fintech products

• A track record of shipping 0-1 products at scale, beyond prototypes and pilots

• Comfort with financial products that carry genuine complexity - you can become an expert in a new instrument, offering structure, or regulatory regime quickly.

• Experience working with legal, compliance, operations, or other regulated-product stakeholders, and the judgment to know when to push and when to redesign

• Experience working with 3rd-party partners on large-scale projects to deliver a shared product

• Strong product judgment and the ability to turn an ambiguous opportunity into a clear strategy, roadmap, and execution plan

• Ability to operate in unclear, 0-1 situations while sustaining a high quality bar under real time pressure

• Demonstrated history of using research, experimentation, and analytics to guide decision making

• Clear communication and relationship management skills, with experience influencing across highly cross-functional teams and with external partners

• Passion for Robinhood's mission to democratize finance for all, and excitement about opening an asset class that has been closed to most investors

• Experience and proficiency building through the latest AI tools such as Claude Code, Gemini, Cursor, or ChatGPT

• Nice to have - familiarity with private markets or alternatives - closed-end funds, BDCs, interval funds, SPVs, Reg D offerings, or the IPO / ECM process.

What we offer

• Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career

• Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, and equity ownership

• Top tier benefits to fuel your work, including supplemental health insurance, ancillary insurance, and mental health support programs

• Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible employer-paid benefits spending account expenses beyond traditional benefits such as wellness, childcare, learning, and more.

• Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, paid volunteer time off, parental leave, and more!

• Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

• Monthly commuter stipend to help offset in-office commuting costs

In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits.

jobs.description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

The Field Process and Systems Team

At Okta, the Field Process & Systems team serves as the strategic connective tissue between our Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy and the technology and processes that power it. We manage the end-to-end design of GTM workflows, optimize our global tech stack, and deploy scalable operational capabilities across our field organization. Our mission is to eliminate operational friction and accelerate growth by delivering data-backed, scalable process and system solutions. As a member of this team, you will work alongside experts in revenue operations, enterprise systems, and GTM strategy to ensure our tools and workflows allow our field organization to execute with speed and precision.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Manager, Field Process & Systems to serve as an operational problem-solver for our field organization. In this role, you will hold a deep, end-to-end understanding of our GTM technology stack while actively driving initiatives that optimize field performance and eliminate daily friction.

You will combine a "process-first" mindset with strong analytical rigor—using data to identify and quantify operational friction points (such as lead routing breakdowns, deal velocity bottlenecks, and handoffs). Crucially, your analytical findings will directly inform our team’s project prioritization—ensuring we tackle the highest-impact operational gaps aligned with overarching company strategy. Additionally, you will own our team's operational drumbeat: managing project intake and leading our monthly cross-functional stakeholder updates.

What You’ll Be Doing

GTM Tech Stack Mastery

• End-to-End Tech Fluency: Maintain a deep, hands-on understanding of our core GTM technology ecosystem (e.g., Salesforce, Clari, ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Gong, Outreach, etc.) to ensure tools are configured, optimized, and utilized effectively.

• Systems & Workflow Architecture: Design scalable, friction-free system solutions and process enhancements that allow sales and revenue teams to execute efficiently.

• Tool Adoption & Best Practices: Ensure high utilization and proper execution across our tech stack by establishing clear process documentation, user guidelines, and operational standards for field teams.

Data-Driven Friction Hunting & Strategic Alignment

• Identify & Quantify Inefficiencies: Leverage system telemetry, CRM data, and operational metrics to uncover field bottlenecks (e.g., lead routing delays, stage-gating friction, and handoff misalignments) and calculate their real business impact.

• Shape Strategy & Prioritization: Use data-backed findings to directly inform what our team prioritizes—balancing quantified operational needs against overarching company strategy to build a high-impact roadmap.

• Propose & Lead System Solutions: Translate operational gaps into concrete, end-to-end system and process proposals, leading execution from concept to close to eliminate friction.

Governance, Intake & Backlog Prioritization

• Manage Project Intake: Take ownership of the Field Process & Systems project intake framework, evaluating incoming requests, system enhancements, and process change proposals from field leadership and business partners.

• Impact-Driven Prioritization: Rigorously evaluate and rank incoming work based on quantified friction, estimated ROI, and strategic business goals to maintain a clear, transparent project backlog.

Stakeholder Management & Operational Cadence

• Lead Monthly Stakeholder Syncs: Own the operational drumbeat for our key initiatives—preparing agendas and decks, leading monthly cross-functional update calls with key stakeholders, and delivering recaps and action items.

• Cross-Functional Visibility: Keep field leadership and key business partners consistently informed on active projects, backlog status, and measurable outcomes from deployed initiatives.

What You’ll Bring to the Role

• 5+ Years of Experience: Background in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, GTM Process Strategy, or Systems Optimization within a fast-paced SaaS environment.

• GTM Tech Stack Expertise: Deep, hands-on fluency with Salesforce and standard GTM technologies (e.g., Clari, ZoomInfo, Gong, LeanData/routing engines).

• Data-Driven & Analytical Acumen: Proven ability to query, analyze, and translate complex operational data into quantified business cases that directly drive roadmap prioritization.

• Structured Intake & Prioritization: Demonstrated success managing project intake frameworks, grooming backlogs, and balancing competing requests against strategic business priorities.

• Cadence & Presentation Mastery: Strong executive presence and communication skills, with proven experience designing polished slide decks and leading cross-functional stakeholder meetings.

• Process-First Mindset: Ability to look beyond quick fixes to build scalable, long-term workflows that reduce friction for field reps while preserving data integrity.
